title: Population integrity, control totals and reconciliations
original_automation_ids: AUTO-001 AUTO-002 AUTO-003 AUTO-004 AUTO-005 AUTO-008 AUTO-011 AUTO-016 AUTO-022 AUTO-031
standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 510; source import contracts
question: What reconciliation proves transfer integrity, and what independent evidence addresses completeness?
research_steps: Define extraction scope, source counts, signed debit/credit totals, row grain and disjoint accepted/quarantined/excluded sets. | Research identifier uniqueness, historical master validity, opening balances and joined-table cardinality. | Write count and amount bridges by entity/period/currency; specify tolerances and residual treatment.
input_contract: Source manifest; original row IDs; certified totals; statuses; exclusions; entity/period/currency/sign/scale.
independent_expected_work: Independent small population with omitted, duplicated, null, negative and quarantined rows; totals recomputed outside application. Balanced bridge must still disclose source-extract completeness limit.
unsupported_or_judgment: Never coerce malformed values to zero, delete suspect duplicates or call an internally balanced extract complete.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Exact original rows; independent count/control evidence; entity/period/currency/scale; accepted/quarantined/excluded dispositions.
algorithm: ["Preserve raw rows and source keys before conversion", "Parse explicit amount/date/sign schemas and reject ambiguous values", "Reconcile source count = accepted + quarantined + excluded, and per-currency signed totals including unresolved quantities", "Reconcile TB opening + debits - credits = closing and GL debit/credit movements independently; certify completeness only to the evidenced extract boundary"]
judgment: Source completeness, appropriate exclusions, tolerances and intended use require actual auditor approval.
exceptions: ["Balanced incomplete extract", "Duplicate business keys", "Unknown amount cannot enter complete total", "Mixed currencies or incompatible scales"]
example: Rows 100,-20,0 CU total80 CU across3 rows. Certified4 rows/80 CU still fails count even though amounts agree.

title: Allocations, adjustments and financial statement bridges
standards_to_verify: Applicable IAS 1/IFRS 18, IAS 8, IAS 7 and disclosure standards; ISA 500
question: How can source rows contribute to statements and notes without duplicate economic effects?
research_steps: Specify source grain and mapping coefficients, residuals, account splits, overlapping presentation and controlled many-to-many links. | Research adjustment/posting/reversal and comparative restatement rules; distinguish linked presentation from financial aggregation. | Define cast/cross-cast and statement/note/cash-flow bridges with materiality-independent integrity checks.
input_contract: Approved TB/GL; mappings; allocation basis; journals; statement/node graph; period/currency.
independent_expected_work: Split one source amount between destinations, then show it in a note: financial total unchanged; adjustment/reversal applied once. Independent line-level bridge identifies every difference.
unsupported_or_judgment: A balancing plug or forced allocation cannot hide unknown mapping; IFRS Taxonomy tags alone do not prove correct recognition/presentation.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Primary allocation and statement bridge v1
inputs: Reviewed source balances; primary allocations; separate note references; signed adjustments; statement node definitions.
algorithm: ["Allocate each source amount to primary destinations using exact amounts or rational coefficients", "Require primary allocated total to equal source; report residual rather than plug", "Apply each approved journal once by immutable identity and period", "Resolve acyclic statement sums; repeated note references display values without increasing primary financial totals"]
judgment: Accounting classification, comparative restatement, current/noncurrent and cash-flow presentation are reviewed elections.
exceptions: ["Over-allocation", "Cyclic statement reference", "Missing source", "Duplicate journal identity", "Unapproved offsetting"]
example: 100 CU ->60 current/40 noncurrent; note100 is a presentation reference. Primary total100, not200 CU.

title: Materiality and clearly trivial thresholds
standards_to_verify: ISA 320, 450; approved firm policy
question: Which values are computed and which choices require professional judgment?
research_steps: Research benchmark selection/normalization, qualitative circumstances, performance and specific materiality, and revision. | Compare source percentage examples with actual standard requirements and firm policy; record policy authority. | Specify precision, zero/negative bases, absolute versus relative inputs, override rationale and dependency staleness.
input_contract: Reviewed benchmark source; selected value; authorized percentages/amounts; framework/period; rationale.
independent_expected_work: Independent workbook for each approved policy; negative profit, exceptional items, zero clearly-trivial threshold, revised benchmarks and boundary rounding. Test historical source values only under documented assumptions.
unsupported_or_judgment: No universal benchmark/percentage or automatic materiality judgment; clearly trivial is distinct from not material.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Benchmark source/value; explicit percentage or amount; specific levels; performance/trivial values; currency/scale; rationale.
algorithm: ["Use an approved normalized benchmark; never take absolute profit silently", "Calculate selected benchmark x rate with explicit final rounding", "Keep specific materiality, performance materiality and clearly trivial distinct", "Version revisions and identify affected samples, evaluation and reporting uses"]
judgment: Benchmark/normalization/percentages and qualitative materiality are professional judgments, not ISA-prescribed constants.
exceptions: ["Negative/zero benchmark", "Blank versus zero trivial", "Rounding boundary", "Revised benchmark"]
example: Illustrative1000000 CU x5%=50000 CU overall;60% of overall=30000 CU performance; explicitly selected trivial0 remains0 CU.

title: Sampling frame and reproducible selection
standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 530; approved sampling policy
question: Which unit/probability frame does each selector implement?
research_steps: Compare random, systematic, haphazard, targeted, stratified and value-weighted approaches for actual offering. | Research algorithm version, deterministic replay, random-byte-to-index bias, unit deduplication, ordering and seed governance. | Specify treatment of selected high-value items, negative/zero monetary units and changed populations.
input_contract: Approved population/version; unique unit ID; design; strata; seed/random source; algorithm version.
independent_expected_work: Independently enumerated tiny frames validate eligibility, unit uniqueness and deterministic replay; technical distribution/bias checks are proportionate to algorithm. Changing source creates a new design.
unsupported_or_judgment: Reproducible HMAC selection is not itself proof of a statistical sampling plan, independence assumptions or confidence evaluation.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Reproducible simple random selection without replacement
inputs: Stable ordered unique eligible IDs; frame hash; n; entropy/seed; exact existing selector version; specific/excluded strata.
algorithm: ["Keep current HMAC/rejection/partial-Fisher-Yates implementation and its inputs", "Partition specific, residual and excluded units disjointly", "Draw n unique residual units without replacement; retain exact order and input basis", "Extensions retain earlier selected prefix and tested-unit lineage under the same frame; changed frame requires new design"]
judgment: Audit objective, unit and design appropriateness require review. Reproducibility is not assurance.
exceptions: ["Duplicate unit IDs", "n>N", "Changed frame", "Missing selected support", "Targeted-only items"]
example: Residual IDs A,B,C; n=3 -> all three exactly once. n=4 is invalid. Same pinned selector inputs reproduce its actual order.

title: Audit sample-size determination
standards_to_verify: ISA 530; approved original statistical references and firm policy
question: Which sample-size approach is justified for controls or substantive testing?
research_steps: Research assumptions for population, expected error/deviation, tolerable misstatement/deviation, sampling risk and finite frame. | For selected statistical methods obtain original formula/table/model and explain distributional assumptions; compare independent reference values. | For nonstatistical design document human rationale and factors; specify full-population escalation and unsupported combinations.
input_contract: Purpose; population; risk; expected error; tolerable amount/rate; strata; reliance; selected method.
independent_expected_work: Independent reference table or separately coded computation over approved parameter grid; monotonicity and impossible-risk/size cases. Manual size retains rationale and reviewer.
unsupported_or_judgment: Generic opinion-poll sample-size formulas or n=30 rules cannot substitute for an audit method. No unsourced confidence claims.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Bounded attribute size helper + evidenced substantive-size route
inputs: N where finite; tolerable deviation p; sampling risk alpha; acceptance count c; expected-deviation rationale; statistical design.
algorithm: ["For binomial zero-acceptance c=0 use smallest integer n with (1-p)^n<=alpha", "For general c use smallest n with cumulative Binomial(n,p) at c<=alpha; expected deviation informs the approved acceptance design, not a hidden formula", "For finite simple random sampling use exact hypergeometric cumulative probability at the declared minimally unacceptable defect count; record threshold rounding", "Substantive/MUS sizes require a separately evidenced matching design/evaluation method; do not apply attribute formulas to money"]
judgment: Selected risk, tolerable deviation, acceptance plan and adequacy are professional methodology decisions; this helper is a proposed bounded design.
exceptions: ["p/alpha outside(0,1)", "n above population", "Expected deviations incompatible with zero-acceptance plan", "Monetary projection requested from attribute plan"]
example: Fictional binomial alpha=.05,p=.05,c=0 gives n=59; .95^58>.05 and .95^59<=.05.

title: Projection, sampling evaluation and risk allowance
standards_to_verify: ISA 530, 450; selected sampling methodology
question: What population does each estimator describe and how is sampling risk evaluated?
research_steps: Research ratio/difference and selected MUS/stratified estimators; define signed book/audited/error amounts and separate specifics. | Specify total projected versus incremental unsampled effect, anomalies, missing tests and replacement conditions. | Research method-specific allowance/confidence calculation separately from point estimation and from booking an adjustment.
input_contract: Approved design; all selected/tested units; audited values; error types; strata; specifics; currency.
independent_expected_work: Independent ratio example: eligible CU1,000, sampled CU200, signed error CU10 gives total CU50 only under approved ratio assumptions; do not add same CU10 again. Test zero/mixed-sign/untested/strata cases.
unsupported_or_judgment: Ratio illustration supplies no confidence bound; controls deviations are not monetary misstatements; anomaly exclusions require auditor evidence.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Point projection with explicit risk-evaluation boundary
inputs: Current reconciled residual frame; tested book/audited amounts; selected projection profile; separately tested specifics; strata.
algorithm: ["Require actual evaluated work on every selected item", "Under existing positive-book same-direction ratio profile compute inclusive residual estimate = residualBook x sampledSignedError / sampleBook", "Incremental projection = inclusive estimate - sampled factual errors; retain factual errors separately", "Sum disjoint strata/specific effects once; record sampling-risk evaluation and additional work independently; no invented confidence bound"]
judgment: Projection method, anomaly classification, sampling-risk allowance and acceptable audit basis require methodology review.
exceptions: ["Mixed-sign errors outside current profile", "Zero sample-book denominator", "Untested item", "Anomaly without evidence", "Population replacement"]
example: 1000 CU residual,200 sampled,10 error ->50 inclusive,40 incremental+10 factual. Separate specific error10 ->60 CU total.

title: Analytical expectations, ratios, trends and tolerances
standards_to_verify: ISA 520, 315, 330, 570; approved policy
question: Which expectation and precision make an analytical comparison useful?
research_steps: Research planning analytics versus substantive analytical procedures and final review. | Specify comparable periods, seasonal/volume drivers, independent nonfinancial data, expected value and acceptable difference. | Compare absolute/percentage/ratio/trend algorithms, denominator failure, disaggregation and corroboration of explanations.
input_contract: Period-aligned population; expectation source; drivers; threshold basis; review and explanations.
independent_expected_work: Independent data with zero/negative denominator, seasonality, offsetting subgroups and missing periods. Explainable flags route to investigation, not an automatic conclusion.
unsupported_or_judgment: Variance threshold is a policy parameter; a ratio flag cannot establish misstatement, fraud or going-concern outcome.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Comparable period/unit inputs; approved expectation; precision; absolute/relative threshold; denominator definition; reliable-data evidence.
algorithm: ["Separate risk-assessment, substantive and final analytical purposes", "Calculate actual-expected difference and ratio under explicit sign/denominator definitions", "Freeze substantive expectation/precision/threshold before observed comparison", "Generate distinct investigation cases with actual explanation and corroboration; preserve historical explanations on refresh"]
judgment: Suitability, reliable data, sufficiently precise expectation, threshold and interpretation remain auditor decisions.
exceptions: ["Zero denominator", "Incomparable periods", "Negative base percentage", "Missing corroboration", "Expectation chosen after seeing actual"]
example: Expected100 CU,actual120 ->difference20 CU and20% using expected100 as denominator. Expected0 ->relative difference not evaluable.

title: Journal-entry and anomaly rules
standards_to_verify: ISA 240, 315, 330, 500; approved fraud-response policy
question: Which indicators warrant testing, and at what journal/line grain?
research_steps: Research journal population completeness and risk-based criteria under applicable fraud edition. | Specify whole-entry balance, split lines, unusual dates/users/accounts, rule overlap and authorized exceptions. | Evaluate false positives, source-system timestamps and actual investigation/evidence obligations.
input_contract: Complete journal header/line population; accounts/users/calendar; selected rule version; investigation evidence.
independent_expected_work: Independent small journals where several rules flag one event; one factual exposure with several indicators. Reversal, legitimate unusual entry and changed criteria cases.
unsupported_or_judgment: No Benford/anomaly score or passed rule set certifies fraud presence/absence. Risk thresholds require policy justification.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Complete reconciled journal lines; journal/line IDs; posting date/time; preparer/approver; accounts; signed amounts; approved rule parameters.
algorithm: ["Validate population and journal balancing before filtering", "Apply explicit rules such as period-end, round amount, unusual account pair, preparer/approver conflict or missing approval using only supplied facts", "Consolidate reasons by journal/line economic unit without multiplying exposure", "Record selection rationale, actual test/evidence, conclusion and finding link; preserve completeness limitation"]
judgment: Fraud risk, rule thresholds, unusualness and final conclusions require human inquiry/investigation.
exceptions: ["No timestamp", "System user different from human author", "Same journal triggers several rules", "Partial journal extract"]
example: One500 CU journal flagged by3 rules ->one candidate,3 reasons,500 CU exposure; no fraud verdict.

title: Receivables aging and subsequent-cash application
standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 505, 540; IFRS 9 and applicable contractual terms
question: Which date and cash-allocation rules produce an auditable aging schedule?
research_steps: Research invoice/due date, reporting-date aging buckets, credit balances, disputed invoices, unapplied cash and partial receipts. | Specify many receipts to many invoices with approvals and prevent reuse of one receipt. | Separate aging/past-due indicators and subsequent receipt evidence from IFRS 9 ECL or confirmation sufficiency.
input_contract: Invoice/open items; due terms; cutoff date; receipts; allocation keys; currencies; reversals.
independent_expected_work: Independent invoices across bucket boundaries, partial/multi-invoice receipts, credit notes and postperiod cash; reconcile opening/closing balance and unapplied remainder.
unsupported_or_judgment: Aged days do not automatically select an ECL rate; cash after date does not alone establish original recognition or complete recoverability.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: As-of aging and explicit receipt allocation
inputs: Invoice/credit/receipt identities; due date or explicitly selected invoice-date basis; report date; signed open amount; referenced cash allocations.
algorithm: ["Reconstruct open balance at reporting date, retaining later receipts separately", "Compute age from selected date basis and assign one mutually exclusive bucket", "Allocate each subsequent receipt to explicit invoice IDs without exceeding receipt/open balance; retain unapplied cash/FX", "Reconcile aging totals to receivable population and evaluate corroboration and recoverability separately"]
judgment: Due-date basis, disputed credit allocation, confirmation alternatives and collectability are auditor decisions.
exceptions: ["Missing due date", "Credit balances", "Partial or duplicate receipt allocation", "Receipt after evaluation cutoff", "Wrong currency"]
example: Invoice100 CU; explicit subsequent receipt40 ->supported receipt40,remaining60 CU. Receipt is not subtracted from the year-end book balance.

title: Revenue and deferred-revenue schedules
standards_to_verify: IFRS 15 or separate selected SME revenue sections; ISA 240, 500, 540
question: What contractual judgments precede each revenue calculation?
research_steps: Research contract/performance obligations, transaction price, variable consideration, standalone prices, modifications and point/over-time criteria. | Specify supported progress/output/input method, contract asset/liability and receivable distinctions. | Document returns, principal/agent, significant financing and specialized cases as conditional research rather than automatic scope.
input_contract: Approved contract facts; obligations; allocation basis; dates; progress evidence; estimates/policy.
independent_expected_work: Independent two-obligation allocation and schedule, advance receipt, partial performance, returns and modification. Reconcile contract balances with approved GL.
unsupported_or_judgment: Equal monthly recognition is not universal; invoice/cash date cannot automatically determine IFRS 15 recognition.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Approved time-based revenue schedule and separate recognition record
inputs: Contract/obligations; approved transaction price and allocation; performance evidence; start/end; period; time/progress convention; recorded revenue.
algorithm: ["Record contract/performance-obligation, price/allocation and over-time versus point-in-time judgments first", "For uniform time-based supported obligations calculate overlap using explicitly full-month or actual-day convention", "Reconcile opening contract liability + applicable receipts/billings - earned release to closing using declared balance signs", "Nonuniform progress/modifications/variable price use an explicitly supported separate method or actual external schedule review"]
judgment: A schedule is arithmetic support; enforceable contract, control transfer, progress, principal/agent and constraint judgments remain recorded professional work.
exceptions: ["Nonuniform performance", "Contract modification", "Inclusive-day versus month mismatch", "Nonrefundable receipt before recognition criteria"]
example: Approved uniform1200 CU/12 full months;3 completed months ->300 CU. Receipt1200 does not alone establish1200 CU revenue.

title: Revenue cut-off, prices, discounts and credit notes
standards_to_verify: IFRS 15; ISA 240, 500, 530; approved contracts
question: Which operational dates and contractual conditions support the tested revenue?
research_steps: Research control transfer using terms, dispatch/delivery/service evidence, returns and postperiod credits. | Specify approved price/discount versions, quantity/unit conversion, taxes, currency and exception tolerances. | Keep cut-off/pricing indicators separate from final recognition judgments and evidence sufficiency.
input_contract: Sales lines; contract/price lists; dispatch/receipt/service dates; credit notes; tax/FX basis.
independent_expected_work: Independent before/on/after-period examples, authorized discount, partial delivery, backdated invoice and later return; one underlying event finding.
unsupported_or_judgment: Window length and anomaly thresholds are audit/firm choices, not universal IFRS/ISA values.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Invoice lines; quantity/unit; approved dated price/discount/tax terms; delivery/control evidence; posting/invoice/credit dates; reporting cutoff.
algorithm: ["Compute expected net line value under explicit sequential/combined discount policy", "Compare commercial arithmetic with recorded amount separately from revenue recognition", "Flag mismatched operational/accounting dates under the approved transaction/control rule", "Link later credits to exact invoices and evaluate whether they corroborate year-end conditions"]
judgment: Delivery terms/control transfer, contract enforceability and adjustment versus subsequent event require actual evaluation.
exceptions: ["Invoice date alone", "Partial delivery", "Price currency mismatch", "Discount tax-base order", "Unlinked credit"]
example: 10 units x20 CU with10% approved discount ->180 CU before declared tax. Dec31 invoice/Jan2 control transfer ->cut-off candidate, not automatic misstatement.

title: Procure-to-pay matching, accruals and unrecorded liabilities
standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 505, 530; applicable accrual/IAS 37/IFRS 9 requirements
question: What relationships and date evidence identify unrecorded or mismatched obligations?
research_steps: Research PO/receipt/invoice/payment line cardinality, partial deliveries, deposits, tolerances and supplier identity exceptions. | Specify accrual periods and search for unrecorded liabilities using postperiod records and actual receipt/service evidence. | Separate duplicate exposure indicator from factual duplicate payment or legal liability conclusion.
input_contract: PO/receipt/invoice/payment lines; supplier masters; dates; service periods; currencies and sign.
independent_expected_work: Independent partial three-way match, duplicate invoice number across suppliers, unbilled receipt, prepaid expense and postperiod payment. Reconcile unresolved values once.
unsupported_or_judgment: No PO does not prove invalid expense; similarity alone cannot establish fraud or an unrecorded obligation.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: PO/receipt/invoice/payment line identities; quantities; supplier/master IDs; service period; posting/payment dates; amount/currency; policy.
algorithm: ["Match explicit stable document-line keys with one-to-many quantities/payments without header multiplication", "Reconcile purchase/payable movements and detect exact duplicates/shared normalized identity candidates", "Compute eligible service-period accrual/prepayment under approved allocation; retain unsettled balances", "Search post-period documents/payments for pre-period obligations and record actual investigation"]
judgment: Receipt/service obligation, appropriate matching tolerance, shared-identity relationship and completeness are human decisions.
exceptions: ["One invoice paid twice versus partial payments", "PO absent but valid expense", "Unmatched service period", "Accrual reversal double count"]
example: Invoice100 CU paid60+40 ->settled100 once. Two invoice lines matching one PO header must not each replicate header100.

title: Bank reconciliation and cash movements
standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 505; IAS 7, IAS 21 where applicable
question: What controlled matching and reconciliation support the cash balance?
research_steps: Research ledger/bank sign, opening/closing controls, clearing dates, bank fees, transfers and reconciling items. | Specify exact/proposed many-to-many matches, partial amounts, approved tolerances and unmatched items. | Retain bank evidence identity and confirmation control; distinguish matching from cash-equivalent classification/restriction.
input_contract: Bank statement/GL; balance controls; transaction IDs; dates/currencies; approved matches.
independent_expected_work: Independent outstanding cheque/deposit, duplicate bank line, interbank transfer, fee and FX item; row/amount residuals reconcile.
unsupported_or_judgment: Matched rows do not prove bank authenticity, ownership, unrestricted cash or absence of omitted accounts.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Signed bank reconciliation and explicit matching
inputs: Independent bank statement; cash GL; exact account/currency/date; bank-reconciliation items with signs/status; transfers; confirmations.
algorithm: ["Match explicit references or approved exact keys; retain ambiguous one-to-many matches", "Recalculate adjusted bank and adjusted book sides with declared sign conventions", "Trace reconciling items to later clearing and investigate stale/unusual items", "Pair inter-account transfers only on supported references; a paired event has two cash legs but one investigation exposure"]
judgment: Bank authenticity, account rights/restrictions, completeness and clearing evidence require evaluation.
exceptions: ["Offsetting unexplained items", "FX mismatch", "Duplicate bank line", "Old outstanding cheque", "Transfer across reporting cutoff"]
example: Bank100 CU +deposit in transit20 -outstanding cheque5 =adjusted115 CU; book115 ->residual0, yet reconciling evidence still required.

title: Inventory movement, count and cut-off
question: Which physical/recorded unit and timing bridges are required?
research_steps: Research count attendance, floor-to-sheet/sheet-to-floor, location/ownership, third-party stock and count-date roll-forward/back. | Specify quantity units, transfers in transit, count adjustments, receipts/issues, duplicate count sheets and signs. | Separate count existence/condition work from costing and NRV.
input_contract: Item/location/lot; count records; units; movements; ownership terms; period dates.
independent_expected_work: Independent count at different date, transfer between sites, negative count adjustment and consignment; quantity bridge before valuation.
unsupported_or_judgment: A reconciled inventory file or uploaded count sheet is not evidence that attendance and physical procedures occurred.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Item/location/unit; opening quantity; dated receipts/issues/transfers; signed count; count date/report date; ownership evidence.
algorithm: ["Reconcile quantity opening +in -out =closing by item/location/unit", "Compare actual signed count with register and record both-direction test evidence", "Roll counts forward/back with actual intervening movements", "Link transfers at both locations and investigate timing/ownership/cut-off rather than treating internal movement as purchase/sale"]
judgment: Attendance, count instructions, ownership, consignment and reliability remain actual audit work.
exceptions: ["Incompatible units", "Unobserved locations", "Negative stock", "Missing transfer leg", "Count date differs from report date"]
example: Opening10+receipts5-issues8=closing7 units;count6 ->register overstatement1 unit before valuation.

title: Inventory cost and cost of sales
standards_to_verify: IAS 2 or separate SME inventory sections; approved accounting policy
question: Which cost formula and overhead treatment apply to each inventory class?
research_steps: Research specific identification, FIFO and weighted average applicability, consistency and periodic versus perpetual calculations. | Specify purchase/conversion costs, normal capacity/overhead allocation, rebates, returns, freight, WIP and negative-stock boundaries. | Define item/location/currency units, rounding level and movements-to-COS bridge.
input_contract: Opening layers; receipts/issues; eligible costs; quantities; selected cost policy.
independent_expected_work: Synthetic vector: 100 units at CU10 plus 50 at CU14, issue 120; FIFO issue CU1,280/closing CU420; periodic weighted average issue CU1,360/closing CU340 before policy rounding. Independently verify additional cases.
unsupported_or_judgment: Weighted average timing matters; production costing cannot be claimed from a simple trading-stock formula. IAS 2 does not permit arbitrary method substitution.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: Periodic weighted-average costing v1; separate additional profiles
inputs: Opening quantity/value; approved eligible receipt/conversion cost; issues/closing quantities; cost method; recorded COS/closing value.
algorithm: ["Reconcile quantities before costing", "Supported periodic weighted average =eligible cost available /units available; retain rational unit cost until declared issue-total rounding", "Compute issue cost then residual closing value so total eligible cost reconciles exactly", "Specific identification/FIFO/moving average/production overhead need their own profile when required; no silent conversion of all clients to weighted average"]
judgment: Permitted cost formula, eligible cost, normal capacity, abnormal waste and policy consistency require reviewed basis.
exceptions: ["No units with nonzero cost", "Negative quantities", "Unsupported fractional units", "Production overhead unsupported", "Method change"]
example: 10 units/100 CU +10/140 ->20 units/240,average12. Issues15 ->180 CU;closing5 ->60 CU.

title: Inventory NRV and obsolescence indicators
standards_to_verify: IAS 2; ISA 540, 500
question: How are estimated selling prices and sale/completion costs corroborated?
research_steps: Research item/group basis, postperiod sales evidence, damaged/obsolete stock, write-down and reversal conditions. | Specify approved estimates, completion/selling costs and lower-of-cost/NRV comparison. | Distinguish slow-moving flags from a supportable valuation conclusion.
input_contract: Costed items; quantities; selling evidence; completion/selling cost assumptions; previous write-downs.
independent_expected_work: Independent inventory with cost above/below NRV, partial sales evidence, negative estimated proceeds and constrained reversal.
unsupported_or_judgment: No universal age bucket/write-down percentage; approved estimates and applicable policy remain necessary.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
profile: NRV input comparison and movement indicators
inputs: Item cost/quantity; approved selling price; completion cost; necessary selling cost; observable evidence date; movement/age thresholds.
algorithm: ["Calculate approved NRV per unit =selling price -completion cost -necessary selling cost", "Compare at supported item or justified grouping level; do not offset unrelated item gains and losses", "Calculate proposed write-down =max(0,cost-NRV) xquantity under supported nonnegative scope", "Flag slow/nonmoving items independently; review reversals subject to original write-down limit and current evidence"]
judgment: Estimated selling price/costs, grouping, obsolescence and reversals require professional evidence; turnover alone is not NRV.
exceptions: ["Missing completion cost", "Negative NRV requiring separate obligation analysis", "Post-period price changes", "Unrelated item netting"]
example: Cost12 CU,price11,completion1,selling1 ->NRV9;5 units ->write-down15 CU.

title: Asset roll-forward, disposals and revaluation movements
standards_to_verify: IAS 16, IAS 38, IAS 36; relevant IAS 40/IFRS 5 only if applicable
question: Which cost, accumulated charge and carrying-value movements must reconcile?
research_steps: Research additions, disposals, transfers, impairments, revaluations and held-for-sale changes by asset class. | Specify register-to-GL reconciliation, component identity and disposal gain/loss evidence. | Separate movement arithmetic from recognition, life/revaluation judgment and title inspection.
input_contract: Asset/component register; opening balances; movements; disposal proceeds; accumulated charges; GL.
independent_expected_work: Independent addition/partial disposal/transfer with cost and accumulated depreciation bridges; carrying value and GL reconcile separately.
unsupported_or_judgment: A balanced asset register cannot certify asset existence, rights or correct capitalization.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Asset/component identity; cost and accumulated charge openings; additions/disposals/transfers/revaluation; impairment; ledger.
algorithm: ["Reconcile gross cost and accumulated depreciation/amortization separately", "Preserve disposal of original cost and related accumulated charge, not net carrying value only", "Compute carrying amount after separately recorded impairment/revaluation effects", "Reconcile movements/classes to ledger and evidence; retain actual disposal consideration and gain/loss support"]
judgment: Recognition, revaluation class policy, derecognition date and classification remain human decisions.
exceptions: ["Disposed cost without accumulated removal", "Asset transferred twice", "Revaluation across only selected class items", "Negative remaining basis"]
example: Cost1000+add200-dispose100=1100;accum300+charge100-remove30=370 ->carrying730 CU before impairment.

title: Depreciation and amortization
standards_to_verify: IAS 16, IAS 38, IAS 8; selected policy
question: Which method, component, service dates and estimate changes govern the charge?
research_steps: Research straight-line, reducing-balance/units-of-production if applicable, components, residual value and available-for-use rules. | Specify daily/monthly conventions, leap years, disposals, idle/fully-depreciated assets, life changes and indefinite-life intangibles. | Separate prospective estimate changes from policy/error corrections and test floors/rounding.
input_contract: Cost; residual; life; method; component; service/disposal dates; prior charge; policy version.
independent_expected_work: Synthetic whole-year straight-line CU120 cost, CU20 residual, five-year life gives CU20 charge; separately test first/last periods, revised life and cumulative floor with independent schedule.
unsupported_or_judgment: No automatic useful-life selection or tax-depreciation substitution; a formula passing does not approve capitalization.
lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
inputs: Cost/component; residual; useful life; available-for-use/disposal dates; reporting window; prior accumulated charge; actual days/month convention.
algorithm: ["Annual base =(cost-residual)/usefulLife for supported cost model", "Apply approved actual eligible period convention; distinguish available-for-use from purchase/payment date", "Cap charge to remaining depreciable carrying basis and retain over-depreciation as a separate exception", "Finite-life amortization uses its own life/support; indefinite-life intangible is not mechanically amortized; estimate changes are prospective under reviewed basis"]
judgment: Useful life, residual, consumption method, componentization, ready date and estimate revisions require actual review.
exceptions: ["Zero life", "Residual above cost", "Partial reporting year beyond profile", "Indefinite life", "Fully depreciated but still used"]
example: Cost1000,residual100,life3 years ->annual300 CU. Approved half-year convention ->150 CU;remaining basis100 caps charge100.

title: Capitalization, repairs and borrowing-cost support

algorithm: ["Evaluate curated decision tables under the selected policy/version", "Preserve unknown and justified N/A; do not treat blank as false or favorable", "Distinguish allowed draft actions, positive professional decisions, independent review and irreversible release/disposal guards", "Retain decision inputs/reason/actor/version; changes invalidate affected reliance and direct routes enforce the same controls"]
judgment: Professional judgments remain attributable decisions. Configurable roles cannot waive a nonwaivable rule or required independent review.
exceptions: ["Unknown applicability", "Self-review", "Expired grant", "Stale revision", "Exact retry versus changed payload", "Cross-engagement object"]
example: Required current work8 items;7 reviewed and1 justified N/A ->7/7 applicable reviewed, with N/A shown; this is coverage, not quality or assurance.
